abstract_summary: Real-time monocular human pose estimation is an important sensing component for human-centered intelligent systems. While recent camera-based methods have achieved impressive accuracy, fundamental challenges persist, particularly when visual observations are incomplete, such as during lower-body occlusion or short o...

IV. METHOD
We propose an insole-enhanced framework for real-time
monocular human pose estimation (Fig. 1). The system takes
the standardized output of a real-time visual backbonev b1:T
and a synchronized smart-insole streams 1:T as inputs to pre-
dict a 22-joint SMPL-style root-relative 3D skeleton ˆP1:T =
fθ(vb1:T ,s 1:T ), where ˆPt ∈R J×3 andJ= 22.
A. Part-Decoupled Vision–Pressure–Inertial Fusion Network
The proposed fusion network is motivated by the physical
relationship between the insole signal and the human body.
Since pressure and acceleration from the feet mainly describe
lower-body contact and dynamics, directly concatenating them
with the whole-body visual representation may be suboptimal.
We therefore use a part-decoupled design, as illustrated in
Fig.

pletely isolating the two branches violates the kinetic chain
principle of the human body. The pelvis and lower spine act as
a mechanical bridge;

evidence.excerpt:
The training objective is designed to supervise both frame-
level pose accuracy and temporal motion quality. Since the
output is a continuous root-relative skeleton sequence, only
minimizing the joint position error may still lead to frame-
wise fluctuations or locally distorted limb configurations.
Following standard practices in temporal 3D human pose
estimation [32]–[34], we combine a joint position loss with
first- and second-order temporal smoothness terms, and a
bone-length consistency constraint:
L=L pos +λ vLvel +λ aLacc +λ bLbone.(7)
Here,L pos penalizes joint position errors in the root-relative
skeleton space and provides the main supervision for pose
accuracy.L vel andL acc constrain first- and second-order
temporal differences, respectively, encouraging the predicted
motion to follow the reference dynamics and reducing high-
frequency jitter.L bone preserves local kinematic

We evaluate our method on the new VPPA dataset (Section
III). Three representative real-time visual backbones are eval-
uated: MediaPipe, YOLOPose26, and SAT-HMR. Reference
body poses are obtained from Xsens MVN. All compared
methods use a fixed action-disjoint split where test actions are
unseen during training. For synthetic lower-body occlusion,
we manually mask the bottom 30% of each video frame with

All models are trained on 120-frame windows. The training
and validation windows are sampled with a step size of 5
frames, while testing uses a step size of 1 frame to obtain
dense frame-level predictions. The proposed fusion model uses
two-layer LSTM temporal modules with a hidden dimension
of 256. The upper- and lower-body branches use separate
temporal memories, and the global coordinator predicts resid-
ual updates for both branches. We train the model using
AdamW with cosine learning-rate scheduling and select the
best checkpoint according to validation PA-MPJPE. For fair
comparison, the vision-only temporal baseline and fusion
variants are trained under the same data split, window length,
and evaluation protocol.

Therefore, the real-occlusion actions are not used
as a standard benchmark with clean counterparts, but as a
stress test for practical obstacle-induced visual degradation.
As shown in Table V, the proposed method remains sub-
stantially more robust than the vision-only temporal baseline
under physical occlusion. It reduces MPJPE from 93.17 mm to
62.06 mm, PA-MPJPE from 65.58 mm to 45.79 mm, and jitter
from 178.25 to 94.00m/s 3. These results complement the
synthetic occlusion experiment: the synthetic setting provides
controlled comparison under the same actions, while the real-
occlusion setting verifies robustness under practical obstacle-
induced visual degradation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Held-out Xsens MoCap reference labels, including MoCap-derived stance contact labels rather than insole pressure, corroborate the reported gains across action-disjoint and subject-disjoint splits.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, jitter, and gait metrics computed against held-out Xsens MoCap reference motion, with stance labels derived from MoCap trajectories rather than the insole input.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training against Xsens MoCap reference labels using joint position, temporal smoothness, and bone-length losses.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The reported findings directly support the claims: insole fusion reliably maintains pose estimation during lower-body obstruction and complete dropouts, reduces MPJPE and temporal jitter, and improves gait-related contact estimation across unseen subjects and real occlusion obstacles.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The experimental validation is extensive and rigorous, covering three diverse visual backbones (MediaPipe, YOLOPose26, SAT-HMR), clean conditions, synthetic occlusion, real desk-induced occlusions, and visual dropouts. Ground truth is measured objectively with a commercial 17-sensor Xsens Awinda MoCap system across standard metrics (MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, jitter) and gait-specific biomechanical parameters (stance accuracy derived from MoCap, step distance, cadence), supplemented by cross-subject evaluations and mobile runtime benchmarks.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on separate reference motion capture (17-sensor Xsens Awinda) where stance ground truth is derived from MoCap trajectories rather than insole sensors, across action-disjoint and subject-disjoint held-out splits.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective geometric and dynamic metrics (MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, trajectory jerk jitter) and gait analysis parameters (heel-strike step distance, cadence, and MoCap-derived stance contact labels) compared against held-out Xsens MoCap recordings.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised optimization using AdamW on multi-task loss terms (root-relative joint position loss, temporal velocity/acceleration differences, and bone-length consistency) relative to synchronized Xsens MoCap reference labels.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including the reliance on root-relative skeletons rather than long-term absolute global trajectories due to lack of absolute global yaw reference, the need for wider demographic and activity testing, and remaining validation requirements in downstream clinical or ergonomic tasks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed: visual backbones provide unified 2D/3D/SMPL keypoint representations split into upper- and lower-body branches, the lower branch fuses insole features via an MLP, separate LSTMs handle temporal dynamics, and a global coordinator shares cross-branch residual updates under position, velocity, acceleration, and bone-length loss constraints.
primary.quality_rationale: The study demonstrates high scientific quality with a clear, technically sound method, a well-synchronized novel dataset, solid comparisons against fair vision-only temporal baselines, thorough ablations, and objective ground-truth evaluation using optical/inertial MoCap reference tracking.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces a part-decoupled temporal fusion framework combining monocular visual pose estimators with smart insole sensing (four piezoresistive pressure points and 3-axis acceleration per foot) and provides a synchronized 890K-frame multimodal dataset to improve 3D human pose estimation during lower-body occlusions and visual dropouts.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study demonstrates high scientific quality with a clear, technically sound method, a well-synchronized novel dataset, solid comparisons against fair vision-only temporal baselines, thorough ablations, and objective ground-truth evaluation using optical/inertial MoCap reference tracking.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including the reliance on root-relative skeletons rather than long-term absolute global trajectories due to lack of absolute global yaw reference, the need for wider demographic and activity testing, and remaining validation requirements in downstream clinical or ergonomic tasks.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
